*Exporting Infobip engagement data via Infobip Data Export API*

In marketing, the teams are using Infobip heavily for SMS and other non-standard communication types (Robocalls, IVR, Chat, Whatsapp messaging, etc). As the volume of such comms is increasing, we’re missing the engagement data to assess properly if such communications make sense and how much impact they bring (if they generate impact at all).

Task: create a data export sync from Infobip Data Export API

[https://www.infobip.com/docs/api#customer-engagement/people/create-events-export-request|https://www.infobip.com/docs/api#customer-engagement/people/create-events-export-request|smart-link] 



*Adding new eater feature group to send Profiling features as user traits to Event service*

ML team has been helping the marketing team to create new feature groups for Event service. For example, Profiling updates once a week Driver weekly and monthly online hour features as user traits via Event service in the marketing platforms. The same is done for Riders, where Profiling updates daily or every 4h (depending on the feature) user traits for various ride counts and last ride timestamps.

Adding a new feature group to the Profiling for Event service will enable MarTech data analysts to generate custom user traits for Lifecycle Marketing use cases. The first use case for eaters is to add order counts with Bolt Market and non-Bolt Market providers. 

Task: Add the new eater feature group that would send features as user traits to the Event service.

_Nice to have: If adding a new feature group takes less time than accounted for, maybe we can add a courier feature group as well._

Caught up with [~accountid:602cd4a04890ef0071f47dee] today - some additional background:

{quote}1 - it's not allowed under PL law

2 - we rolled out Community Rules as a response to many cases of sexual harassment done by drivers to riders. We want to make sure that we can block any driver who violates the rules (eg. sexual talk)

3 - we're testing a driver verification feature (to prevent impersonation). We had a lot of cases when driver in the app (verified by us) was different to the actual person driving the car. This feature makes it possible to verify their identity via selfie (real-time) compared to documents in our system{quote}

My take:

1 - all good. This is regulatory matter so we can make it part of our contract.

2 - I understand it comes from security incidents related to sexual harassment, etc. Team developed dedicated guideline around that [https://blog.bolt.eu/pl/zasady-spolecznosci-bolt-bezpieczenstwo-i-komfort-podczas-przejazdu|https://blog.bolt.eu/pl/zasady-spolecznosci-bolt-bezpieczenstwo-i-komfort-podczas-przejazdu|smart-link] . This is essentially a High-priority cases with specific guidance. Its ok to do this in general, but the currently proposed wording does not seem to be in line with P2B Regulation sec. 4(4) rules which allow to immediately terminate account without a standard 30 day notice.

Hence, what we need to do is either: i) adjust the wording and process so that we only block drivers for “repeated” breach of the guidelines OR ii) get comfortable that immediate termination for breach of guidelines falls under sec. 4(4)a or 4(4)b under Polish law - I know [~accountid:618d2fe286c210006aa6241e] has sought advice from local counsel on similar issue already so maybe we can get comfort from that advice.

If we solve alignment with P2B challenge - its ok to add this wording.

3 - this is a feature deployed by @romain moisescot’s team: visual confirmation of driver. We need to cross-check if privacy angle is sorted ([~accountid:609f85c547ba02006fe1b9c3]  - could you check and confirm this or propose actions to be taken from privacy angle before we launch).



So proposed plan:

once the points 1 and 2 are solved, we need to 

* update proposed T&C drafting

*** with summary of changes

Hello, thanks for reaching out. I try to break down the issue and possible solutions.

_Background_: Citibank (as any other financial institution) is bound by certain legal requirements to comply with sanctions and other financial legislation regarding payments to specific countries, individuals and entities to prevent money laundering, terrorist financing etc. In accordance with these requirements, they might stop our payouts for compliance check. Recent delays come in fact that due to current geopolitical events (mainly war in Ukraine), the scale of the sanctions, and the pace of regulatory changes being implemented (new sanctions are put in place regularly), additional time may be required to complete the review by Citibank due to high workload.

Gradually the situation should stabilize when geopolitical situation will normalize – unfortunately it seems to be still in unforeseen future 

Citibank has informed us they have already put in place measures that would minimize the delays. We will keep pushing them until we start to see significant positive change in terms of that. 

On our side we are working on the solution to mitigate the situation and lower the probability of payout getting stuck in Citibank’s sanctions compliance bureaucracy. Shortly – This involves adding more detailed information regarding our partner to the payment instruction details. The discussion with Citibank regarding which details and where to add are ongoing. After we have clear business requirements gathered, we create a task for our engineers who can apply the changes into payment initiation logic/files. This will happen during Q3.

_What could be done in France?_

Some of the details being checked are beneficiary name (account recipient) and Date of Birth (for persons). To mitigate the situation these details should be clear on drivers profile so these can be automatically sent with payment instruction

* *Beneficiary name* (account recipient) - should contain clear full name without abbreviations, weird characters etc…. 
** When onboarding new drivers apply quality check that this is done like that
* *Date of Birth (DoB)* - can be added in Birthday field on driver’s profile. I pulled some data from Looker and seems that for drivers created in the past 90 days, for around 30% has been DoB added

Actually consent is not required for the recording of calls. The recording is done under legitimate interest and the other party may at any point object to this (i.e. say that they do not wish to be recorded). 

However, we have to inform in the beginning of the call that the call will be recorded and state for what purposes. This can be done by the agent themselves or implementing an automatic script before the call.

So all in all, you can change the approach to start recording right away and if the person objects, then can stop the recording.

Yes, in general this is OK, however some documentation requirements and information requirements would need to be fulfilled for compliance. I checked the German _Datenschutzkonferenz_ 'DSK' [guidelines |https://www.datenschutzkonferenz-online.de/media/oh/20200903_oh_v%C3%BC_dsk.pdf]and they align with our general approach in other markets. 

First I would like to understand and also document the set-up/locations with the cameras that would be installed and the purposes for which they would be used. [~accountid:6038bb05f0327400688a35b0] - please fill in the questionnaire found [here|https://docs.google.com/document/d/16ZnJ3hj5GQZ4BfywghXFQCe-yGo5AJeN06PHo-aUkQg/edit]. Bring out all the premises where cameras will be installed and if they exist (i think yet no) then add to this ticket camera location maps.

Our policy for video surveillance can be found on Confluence[ here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/3489661435/Policy+on+using+video+surveillance+on+the+premises+of+Bolt].

The steps to reach compliance with the cameras installed are the following:

# *Legal basis and purpose of the video surveillance:*
The legal basis for processing data through CCTV is legitimate interest (GDPR art 6 (1) f)). Legitimate interest requires at first step that the purposes of using cameras are identified (this is asked in the questionnaire).
# *Positioning the cameras*
The location and positioning of the video cameras has to take into account the legitimate expectations of the data subject to their privacy. Therefore monitoring is +not to be expected in recreational areas, sanitary areas, changing rooms+ etc.
The positioning of the video cameras should be aimed to record areas which correspond to possible threat (theft, property damage).
# *Audio on cameras*
Audio recording should not be used as this can fall under the criminal offence of Section 201 Paragraph 1 and Paragraph 2 of the Criminal Code.
# *Retention time of the recordings*
The retention time should be limited to what is strictly necessary. I.e. time needed to detect possible thefts/damages/unauthorised access/review safety incidents. The guidelines bring out that “_whether it is necessary to back up the material can be clarified in most cases within one to two working days. That means a storage period of 72 hours in general”._   
After the retention period set the footage must be deleted automatically.
# *Access control and logs*
Access rules must be put in place on who has access to the footage and every access to footage is logged.
# *Transparency and information requirement*
Information/warning signs should be installed with the following information:
-Information that there is video surveillance in the area (e.g camera picture, “We have video surveillance”)
-Controller (“Controller information”)
-Legal basis: Legitimate interest
-Information of where further information can be found (QR code or link to the [global privacy notice on video surveillance|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/terms-for-video-surveillance]). 
We also have a template sign which I can share that could be made to stickers. However I need to understand which entity would be the controller here? Bolt Operations OÜ or Bolt Services DE GmbH? [~accountid:62722e092db308007024a425] can you maybe assist with this? 
# *Data protection agreement with service provider*
If we use third party service providers (for hosting etc) then a DPA must be signed with them. Do we plan to have a service provider for cameras (e.g. for hosting) and what is their role or where do we store the data?

This fraud rule triggers when the user is trying to create an order using a business payment method that belongs to a company with a negative balance. We allow businesses to make orders even if the payment fails, but the increase of the amount in each of these preparation attempts means the payment is failing and we keep adding it to their balance for the next order. And the company becomes high risk.

*What could be done?*

The admin of the company needs to clear the failed payments amount. In other words, the company must pay their debt, and once that is done, the users will be able to use the business payment method *within 24 to 48 hours after the payment is made.*

The non-observance of the health and safety at work regulations in question (i.e. the appointment of the dedicated OHS worker and of the OHS Committee) are considered as administrative offences carrying total fines ranging from RON 11,000 (approx. 2,200 Eur) up to  RON 22,000 (approx. 4,400 Eur), depending on the breaches found.

In addition, as per the Criminal Code:

* the person in charge with taking the health and safety at work legal measures and who fails to take any of such measures, thus determining a serious and imminent danger for occurrence of a work accident or professional disease, may be subject to criminal charges and sanctioned with imprisonment or with criminal fine, 
* the non-observance by any person of the health and safety at work obligations and measures, if such conduct creates a serious and imminent danger for occurrence of a work accident or an occupational disease, represents a criminal offence and may be sanctioned by imprisonment or criminal fine. 

Thus, in case of a work accident, to the extent the labor and criminal authorities conclude that the accident in question was also caused by the company’s failure to comply with the OHS obligations in question, the criminal liability of the company and/ or the management could be triggered.

In addition, the employer could, at least in theory, face tort liability (material and moral damages) in case the employee involved in a working accident would be able to prove in front of the court that the employer failed to comply with one or several health and safety obligations incumbent upon it and thus has caused or essentially contributed to the occurrence of the work accident and of the damages to the employee’s health and physical integrity. 

In reaching a solution, the court could take into account the conclusions of the report issued by the relevant territorial labor inspectorate when concluding the investigation of the working accident as well as the ruling of the criminal court, in case the criminal liability of the employer would be raised.

Please also consider that the dedicated OHS worker and the OHS Committee +must be set up locally, and specifically for the Romanian entity and by using local employees. Thus, the H&S team based in Estonia would not be deemed as a compliant solution from a labor authority perspective and could trigger the types of liabilities mentioned above.+ 

Lastly, to clarify, the labour medicine doctor stands for the occupational physician which is generally concerned with the maintenance of [health|https://www.britannica.com/topic/health] and the prevention and [treatment|https://www.britannica.com/science/therapeutics] of diseases and accidental injuries of employees in the workplace. The company should already have a contractual relationship with such occupational physician who ensures, among others, the periodical medical check up of all employees in order to confirm their medical fitness for the occupied roles.

Please let me know if anyone has any further questions on this? 

Thanks, 

Liisa

Hello Ángela, good afternoon.

Further to the query raised on which company (Bolt Ops vs Local entities) should bear the costs arising from the international expansion of micro – mobility vehicles’ charging stations, we believe that *BOLT’S LOCAL ENTITIES* (1) must be the *legal owners of the charging docks* that may be installed and operated within their corresponding jurisdiction, thus (2) *local entities should bear all costs* arising both from the charging dock’s installation and from their management and recurrent costs.

The reasons behind such a conclusion may be set out as follows:

# Permanent establishment (PE) exposure.

If Bolt Ops is the legal owner of the charging stations deployed abroad the local tax authorities of the countries where the stations are installed may consider that Bolt Ops is running a business activity within their territory by way of a PE which means, in summary, that Bolt Ops would be liable for all material and formal tax liabilities arising from running such business activity in each country where the docks are installed.

Therefore, Bolt Ops must transfer the charging docks to the local entities, without any markup on the acquisition costs borne by Bolt Ops.

# VAT

 

2.1.         +Local VAT on the installation and rental of the land.+

We guess that the land where the charging stations are installed will be rented to local landlords. Such rental will be subject to local VAT that can be ordinarily recovered by the local entities owning the charging stations.

If Bolt Ops was the legal owner of the charging stations deployed outside EE, Bolt Ops would bear local VAT, so the Company would have to go through a complex and highly time–consuming administrative process to apply for the refund of such VAT. Such process would also trigger financial costs because Bolt Ops would have to wait a long time until receiving the funds.

2.2.         +VAT on the transfer of the docks from Bolt Ops to local entities.+

 

·               The transfer of charging stations from Bolt Ops to the EU based local entities qualify as an ordinary intra-community transfer of goods, which is exempted from Estonian VAT. At the local entities level, these transactions qualify as an ordinary intra- community acquisition of goods subject to local VAT, which will be ordinarily recovered by the local entities.

 

·               The transfer of charging stations from Bolt Ops to non - EU based local entities qualify as an exportation of goods, which is exempted from Estonian VAT. Local entities will bear local VAT accrued at importation, but such VAT should be ordinarily recoverable under local VAT regulations.

 

# TRANSFER PRICING (TP)

Under Bolt’s centralized business model, all costs borne by the local entities from the purchase, installation and management of the charging docks will be recharged to Bolt Ops by way of a cost – plus remuneration model.

Under Bolt’s localized business model, all costs borne by the local entities from the purchase, installation and management of the charging docks will be part of the local entities’ costs and expenditures.

Should you require further information or any clarification, don’t hesitate to let us know.

*10 MAJOR DOs AND DON’T OF CUSTOMER SUPPORT*

Very general but useful - it’s more applicable to OS. It speaks more about quality. It is covered in our onboarding but it’s a nice refresher for existing agents. I’d like to see more practice scenarios with this or possibly a live session (team meeting hosted by the TL, for example). _Side note: might be useful for market introductions_

*10 WAYS TO IMPROVE CUSTOMER CONVERSATIONS* 

Multitasking is seen as negative. use open-ended questions (asking the right questions). Nice points: stay engaged and efficient. Focus on solving the issue - don’t keep the customer around for any longer than they have to be there. Components of listening - understanding/emphasizing. Dissecting what the person is saying. Be brief in communication.

*3 SECRET STEPS FOR CONFIDENT CS AGENTS*

Practice: identify customer concerns/answer common questions/walking contacts through the solutions.

Confidence: controlled breathing/ short breaks before responding

*4 WAYS TO FIND MEANINGFUL OPPORTUNITIES IN CS*

* Comes across as jargon in the beginning.
* Might be tricky for agents to grasp at first. An option would be to add or edit bits to help agents understand the topic and how they fit into this
* I like the points in section 5 about solving multiple issues within a single contact. We now have this ability in BH where more than 1 ATI/issue tag can be added. So no issue there in terms of data.

*9 PHRASES TO IMPROVE EVERY SUPPORT INTERACTION*

Pretty decent. There’s a fair amount more to add but these would suffice. Perhaps add a way to put these into practice, like Rise 360 style: Feedback journey questioning.

*BEST PRACTICES FOR PHONE CONVERSATIONS*

* Before calling - need to check if this matches our call procedure/s, like when to answer, etc.
* Watch Your Language - avoid internal terms, like OPS, abbr. etc. Nice phrases that can be used. Perhaps add practical exercise
* The tone of Voice - is self-explanatory
* Active Listening - good tips
* Inform - good tips and examples. Perhaps add practical exercise
* The AWARE Approach - good tips and acronym. Use an example of what this would look like using this acronym.
* Sources - good to have there but might be better to extract info? I fear agents might be discouraged from actually opening the links.

*BEST PRACTICES FOR USING CHATS*

Not really needed here as this is already in place and built by us. However, nice best practices.

*HOW TO WRITE EFFECTIVE BUSINESS EMAILS*

The title is not really fitting as we don’t use actual emails to communicate with customers but the format is used through BH. I would really depend too much on this one.

*FIRST IMPRESSIONS AND INTERACTIONS*

This is a good course but seems to fit a more pre-covid time. Monitoring your distance or hand shaking will be more of a choice nowadays rather than seen as a form of etiquette. Hi Juan,

I had a conversation with Epp Aasaru in the beginning of June about this. She shared the same question you posted here and mentioned it came through you. Back then, I discussed with Epp and I suppose she shared our thoughts with you afterward?

In any case, please see below a quick summary:

* Clause 5.10 Global E-Vehicles Ts&Cs is not referring to refund/withdrawal rights, which by law can be requested by consumers within 14 days in our case. It actually refers to disputing payments/transactions in the context of in-App Payment. I’m not sure if the 10 days are based on payment regulations or if it’s just a deadline agreed internally with finance team.
* Concerning refunds per se, I’d say it’s hard to create a one-size-fits-all solution and, in any case, this should not come from Legal. I explain:
** One thing is a user who actually used Bolt services (took a ride) and is complaining about the experience. This is a user experience topic and Bolt might have business reasons to refund depending on the case.
** Another thing is a user who did not use Bolt services at all (e.g., scooter was not working) and was charged anyway. In this case, in general, Bolt is legally required to refund the user regardless of the timeline, otherwise Bolt is getting paid for something it did not provide. Unless the consumer takes extremely long to reach out to Bolt that even the statute of limitations have elapsed – think of 5 years or more.

Despite this not being a legal topic per se, I checked with CS team and there seems to be no consistent approach regarding user complaints and deadlines. Below I reproduce the feedback received from Sintija Ergle, which I also shared with Epp:

_“Me and_ [_@teodor.parsoaga_|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U03DHQM5DU6] _are currently working on a general Compensation guidelines KB article for Drive. This is still a WIP though, so for now, any compensation directions are actually stored in the specific KB articles (wherever we currently issue any sort of compensations)._[_Here’s the worksheet_|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/10GWqKl4bsJqxvVBeOlasmfv4jeZSyLMj-hi5-_KIEm0/edit#gid=0] _Teo works on, it lists all Drive KB articles and what sort of compensations do we offer. Let me know if you have any questions\!As for other rentals (Scooters and E-bikes), I don’t see one general guide in the KB for the compensations, so it’s likely the same situation as with Drive (compensation instructions are in each KB article if applicable).We don’t have any guidelines for evaluating when the compensation is requested (for Drive for sure, and I’m pretty sure for Rentals, too - although I’d have to confirm). As you mentioned, it’s more of a case-by-case situation at the moment.  I remember some cases where customers reach out even months after some sort of an incident, requesting a refund. Typically I’ve seen CS leads (sometimes with the OPS team’s involvement) helpin with the evaluation whether the request is legitimate.We’ll be discussing the Drive compensations with the Drive OPS team on Monday, after which we’ll be able to work on creating the Drive compensation guidelines for CS agents. We’re evaluating if we can create some sort of a logic based on when the user requests the refund (reservation, ride just started, active ride, long-term ride, ride finished) but I can’t confirm much more at this point.  I’ll share with_ [_@teodor.parsoaga_|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U03DHQM5DU6] _about the requests for issues that happened 1 - … months ago and similar cases.”_

I hope this is useful. Let me know if I can be of further help.

The way Bolt Balance works in different currencies is that let’s say the user is currently in Romania and wants to order in Romania, we  only look at the Romania (ron currency) balance. Hey [~accountid:629e29ebbe336c006fe7347c] 

Most of the markets have the same rules for legal entities in EU - once they hit certain revenue during tax period, they become liable to pay VAT. Since for most markets this limit is set across all driver/fleet activities, Bolt has no way to keep an eye on that (we could monitor our own balances but still a blind spot for any other earnings the driver/fleet/courier might have, for example lots of drivers are active on different ride hailing platforms at the same time). Due to this, the responsibility to let us know when their VAT status has changed, is on the partner.

In case VAT liability changes in the middle of the month, at the moment you’d have to create new profile with new data - no way to split the monthly invoice (same as if driver moves between fleets). If they become liable, for example from 1st of august, you *can* update the current driver profile but it would still be preferable to create new one to keep accounting clean.

There are several cases when we have multiple requests in a row:

# App fold/unfold (2 requests - service availability monitor + parallel orders worker)
# App startup (3 requests - init interactor + service availability monitor + parallel orders worker)


1. In current task I merged service availability monitor and parallel orders worker in {{ServiceAvailabilityWorker}}, which runs in logged-in scope and listens all possible location config refresh triggers: location change, language change, parallel orders invalidation keys change. This way double requests from 2 workers are eliminated.

2. App startup logic refactoring seems to be non-trivial, because there are many entry points to the app (sign up, sign in, deeplinks). Also, double request on app startup is not as severe as double requests on app fold/unfold, since app startups are not as frequent. However, from quick overview, seems that we have some outdated logic in app startup flow, and it would be nice to refactor it. +*Czech Republic*+

below I analyse the possible use of the advertising slogan "Supermarkets' prices, faster delivery" in the Czech Republic and the possible effects of such an advertising campaign in the field of unfair competition law and public law prohibiting deceptive advertising. First of all, it is necessary to state that the use of such a slogan can have both private and public law consequences:

* 

*Private law consequences*

Your promotion campaign may violate the provisions prohibiting unfair competition. This would cause damage to your competitors, who can then claim claims on the basis of your unfair competition. Your competitors may then request that you refrain from unfair competition in the future (i.e. that you will not repeat such a campaign) or that the offending campaign be removed. In addition, reasonable satisfaction, damages and the issuance of unjust enrichment can be demanded. The amount of these claims cannot be calculated in advance, as they depend on the individual conditions of your competitor.

I believe that your proposed campaign slogan may meet the definition of prohibited comparative advertising. This is not an obvious case of a prohibited comparison campaign, but strictly speaking, such a designation can be inferred. I draw such a conclusion from the following. The Czech Civil Code allows comparative advertising only on the condition that all the exhaustively listed conditions are fulfilled. At the same time, it is necessary to take into account the case law of the CJEU.

It follows from the case law of the CJEU (C-381/05) that an advertisement that does not directly designate a specific competitor, but several competitors, can be considered a comparative advertisement, if such a designation makes it possible to know who belongs to this group of competitors. In this case, it can be seen that your comparison refers to all competitors who operate supermarkets in respective market (e.g. Lidl, Kaufland), comparing that you have prices like these competitors. This means that you are in the ad comparison mode and therefore the legal requirements must be met. 

In particular, comparative advertising must not be misleading, and in the proposed case, I believe that advertising in its current form can be considered misleading. I refer to another decision of the CJEU (C‑356/04), where a comparative advertisement comparing the price level of two competitors was assessed, where the following was concluded:

“+_comparative advertising claiming that the advertiser’s general price level is lower than his main competitors’, where the comparison has related to a sample of products, may be misleading when the advertisement:_+

+_–        does not reveal that the comparison related only to such a sample and not to all the advertiser’s products_+_,_

_–        does not identify the details of the comparison made or inform the persons to whom it is addressed of the information source where such identification is possible, or_

_–        contains a collective reference to a range of amounts that may be saved by consumers who make their purchases from the advertiser rather than from his competitors without specifying individually the general level of the prices charged, respectively, by each of those competitors and the amount that consumers are liable to save by making their purchases from the advertiser rather than from each of the competitors._”

In your email it was stated that you only achieved supermarket prices for some products. However, it follows from your slogan that your prices correspond to the prices of supermarkets in general. I consider this to be problematic and contradictory to the aforementioned case law of the CJEU. The proposed slogan can thus be interpreted as misleading.

It is therefore recommended to pay attention to the cited case law of the CJEU and carefully ensure the translation of the slogan into Czech so that the cited conditions are met. Alternatively, it will be necessary to add additional information to the advertisement. For the sake of completeness, I am quoting the provisions of the law that set out all the conditions of permitted comparative advertising:

“_Comparative advertising is permitted in terms of making comparisons in the following cases:_

_a) if it is not misleading,_

_b) if it only compares goods or services which satisfy the same need or which are intended for the same purpose,_

_c) if it objectively compares one or several relevant, important, verifiable and typical properties of goods or services, including_

_price,_

_d) if it compares goods with a designation of origin only to goods of the same designation,_

_e) if it does not disparage a competitor, its position, its activities or its results, or their identification, or unfairly benefits therefrom,_

_and_

_f) if it does not offer goods or services as an imitation or copy of goods or services identified by a trademark of a competitor or by the competitor’s name_.”

* 

*Public law consequences*

The law prohibits the use of deceptive business practices, while this obligation is supervised by the relevant authorities. Act on Consumer Protection No. 634/1992 Coll. stipulates a fine of up to CZK 5,000,000 for a violation of the ban on the use of unfair business practices.

The law prohibits advertising that is an unfair business practice. Advertising Regulation Act No. 634/1992 Coll. stipulates a fine of up to CZK 5,000,000 for violation of this prohibition.

Based on all of the above, I recommend paying attention to the exact wording of the planned campaign so as not to violate the law. Note that comparison advertising is fairly heavily regulated - so I'd consider framing your ad campaign in such a way that you get out of comparison campaign mode. This can be achieved in various ways, for example by reformulating the slogan so that it cannot be related to any particular competitor (in its current form it can be related to supermarket operators).

To sum up, the external counsel found current proposed wording risky in terms of unfair competition regulation. Violation of this regulation may result in a fine of up to CZK 5,000,000.The suggested wording may be found misleading and we might risk claims from our competitors.

Please find the explanations of external counsel below.

----

below I analyse the possible use of the advertising slogan "Supermarkets' prices, faster delivery" in the Czech Republic and the possible effects of such an advertising campaign in the field of unfair competition law and public law prohibiting deceptive advertising. First of all, it is necessary to state that the use of such a slogan can have both private and public law consequences:

*  

*Private law consequences*

Your promotion campaign may violate the provisions prohibiting unfair competition. This would cause damage to your competitors, who can then claim claims on the basis of your unfair competition. Your competitors may then request that you refrain from unfair competition in the future (i.e. that you will not repeat such a campaign) or that the offending campaign be removed. In addition, reasonable satisfaction, damages and the issuance of unjust enrichment can be demanded. The amount of these claims cannot be calculated in advance, as they depend on the individual conditions of your competitor.

I believe that your proposed campaign slogan may meet the definition of prohibited comparative advertising. This is not an obvious case of a prohibited comparison campaign, but strictly speaking, such a designation can be inferred. I draw such a conclusion from the following. The Czech Civil Code allows comparative advertising only on the condition that all the exhaustively listed conditions are fulfilled. At the same time, it is necessary to take into account the case law of the CJEU.

It follows from the case law of the CJEU (C-381/05) that an advertisement that does not directly designate a specific competitor, but several competitors, can be considered a comparative advertisement, if such a designation makes it possible to know who belongs to this group of competitors. In this case, it can be seen that your comparison refers to all competitors who operate supermarkets in respective market (e.g. Lidl, Kaufland), comparing that you have prices like these competitors. This means that you are in the ad comparison mode and therefore the legal requirements must be met. 

In particular, comparative advertising must not be misleading, and in the proposed case, I believe that advertising in its current form can be considered misleading. I refer to another decision of the CJEU (C‑356/04), where a comparative advertisement comparing the price level of two competitors was assessed, where the following was concluded:

“+_comparative advertising claiming that the advertiser’s general price level is lower than his main competitors’, where the comparison has related to a sample of products, may be misleading when the advertisement:_+

+_–        does not reveal that the comparison related only to such a sample and not to all the advertiser’s products_+_,_

_–        does not identify the details of the comparison made or inform the persons to whom it is addressed of the information source where such identification is possible, or_

_–        contains a collective reference to a range of amounts that may be saved by consumers who make their purchases from the advertiser rather than from his competitors without specifying individually the general level of the prices charged, respectively, by each of those competitors and the amount that consumers are liable to save by making their purchases from the advertiser rather than from each of the competitors._”

In your email it was stated that you only achieved supermarket prices for some products. However, it follows from your slogan that your prices correspond to the prices of supermarkets in general. I consider this to be problematic and contradictory to the aforementioned case law of the CJEU. The proposed slogan can thus be interpreted as misleading.

It is therefore recommended to pay attention to the cited case law of the CJEU and carefully ensure the translation of the slogan into Czech so that the cited conditions are met. Alternatively, it will be necessary to add additional information to the advertisement. For the sake of completeness, I am quoting the provisions of the law that set out all the conditions of permitted comparative advertising:

“_Comparative advertising is permitted in terms of making comparisons in the following cases:_

_a) if it is not misleading,_

_b) if it only compares goods or services which satisfy the same need or which are intended for the same purpose,_

_c) if it objectively compares one or several relevant, important, verifiable and typical properties of goods or services, including_

_price,_

_d) if it compares goods with a designation of origin only to goods of the same designation,_

_e) if it does not disparage a competitor, its position, its activities or its results, or their identification, or unfairly benefits therefrom,_

_and_

_f) if it does not offer goods or services as an imitation or copy of goods or services identified by a trademark of a competitor or by the competitor’s name_.”

*  

*Public law consequences*

The law prohibits the use of deceptive business practices, while this obligation is supervised by the relevant authorities. Act on Consumer Protection No. 634/1992 Coll. stipulates a fine of up to CZK 5,000,000 for a violation of the ban on the use of unfair business practices.

The law prohibits advertising that is an unfair business practice. Advertising Regulation Act No. 634/1992 Coll. stipulates a fine of up to CZK 5,000,000 for violation of this prohibition.

Based on all of the above, I recommend paying attention to the exact wording of the planned campaign so as not to violate the law. Note that comparison advertising is fairly heavily regulated - so I'd consider framing your ad campaign in such a way that you get out of comparison campaign mode. This can be achieved in various ways, for example by reformulating the slogan so that it cannot be related to any particular competitor (in its current form it can be related to supermarket operators).

Hello, Team\!

My name is Anton, I am an analyst at Bolt, helping our Ads team organize experiments and interpret the results.
Very nice to meet you and happy you invited us to participate in the experiment\!

I've read through the previous emails and seen the video recording, but I still would like to ask some questions. Would be really glad if you could help us with that.

====

# On target metric

As far as I can see from the recording, we have decided that our target metric will be conversion to installs.
I strongly support this decision, since Ride Finished (especially, First) is a very insensitive metric.

# On conversion tracking

I would like to make sure that Tiktok team will be able to calculate the results correctly, and for this I would like to know which exactly conversions Tiktok get from us.
a) Could you please confirm that you get conversions from us via appsflyer integration
b) Do you receive the amount of installs (I can see that you receive 'First Ride Finished', but am not sure)
c) +and most important:+ in case you get data through integration with Appsflyer, do you only get attributed data (i.e. attributed by appsflyer to bytedanceglobal_int) or do you get all our data?

The c) question is most important because we would like you not to be limited by Appsflyer attribution rules, but to see all the conversions from test and control group.

# On Power Analysis (special thanks for providing that\!)

Below in the thread I can see two Power Analysis scenarios. Thank you for these ones. Below are some questions regarding them:

a) Were these analyses estimated for the 'First Ride Finished' event or for installs already?

b) Can you please say:

# why do you recommend frequency 4?
# why do we have cpm 3.8, is it our benchmark?
# why do you recommend 4 weeks?

c) We have done some back-fo-the-envelope maths to reproduce the power analysis results. We managed to reproduce the calculation for sample size, but we're not sure how to reproduce the cost. Please consider our logic below and say where we are wrong.

+Consider Scenario 1:+
We have 1 878 061 required sample size.
Each user will have frequency 4: 1 878 061 * 4  ~ 7,2kk impressions.
Since CPM is 3.8, for 7,2kk impressions we should pay 7,2kk *3,8Eur / 1000 ~ 27k Eur (not 77k)

Can you please provide your way to calculate it?

d) Did I get it right that per_in_test is the probability to get False positive results? I am asking because I am not sure if we can proceed with these ones. We'd like to have 0.05 at least, but understand that it requires bigger sample size.

e) Can we suggest our own parameters for the test? (i.e. we might think that 15% uplift is not enough and suggest assuming 40% effect)
====

Those are all questions for now.
If there is too much text, we can have another call to discuss the technical details.
(I will be off next Monday, but will be happy to connect any other day)

Thank you and have a good weekend\!

Here are some early notes on my informal audit of the platform:

* Technically the platform seems to be advanced, with automated sample size calculator, segmentation slicing, and even switchback testing enabled
* Definitely concerns over testing practices, in particular there is no visibility on how well users stuck to sample size recommendations (this could be analysed retrospectively) and there are no corrections for multiple comparisons which is troubling given the long list of metrics presented by default
* From talking to a few platform users there seems to be some confusion over the basic aims of testing (common quote: “We struggle to reach statistical significance”)
* The documentation touches on everything, but is not linearly structured so that users can flow through it
* Definite “rubber stamping” behavior going on, with teams using experimentation to just validate their product ideas in reporting, and not for any actual product development
* Most of the above issues sounds like they are being addressed in Q3, in particular with the introduction of a standardized workflow. Whats still missing for me though is an accessible documentation structure that really simplifies the process and puts forward our “philosophy” about what how testing should be done and why the platform is configured as it is. 
* Communication channels seems to be a company-wide pain point, which slack too noisy and confluence not dynamic and has low discoverability. The Experimentation Team could try break the mold here and get creative.
* In sum, platform has impressive technical foundations (likely given the strong engineering focus to date) but some basic elements around usability are missing. Right now its very easy for users to misuse it, and its hard for us to effectively provide feedback and guidance.

_With regard to partial refunds, the only compliant way to do this is to ask user for his/her consent before doing the partial refund to Bolt Balance. As explained in [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/42274|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/42274|smart-link] , the deadlock is caused by the 2 queries below:

{noformat}UPDATE `provider_menu_update_publish_request`
SET status = 'skipped_redundant'
WHERE
  status = 'pending' AND
  id < {id} AND
  provider_id = {providerId}{noformat}

{noformat}UPDATE `provider_menu_update_publish_request`
SET `status` = 'published'
WHERE
  `id` IN ( {ids} )
  AND `status` = 'pending'{noformat}

Even though the result sets are disjoint, the locks can occur on same rows. This is because MySQL's InnoDB locks on examined rows and not on the result rows [\[1]\[2]|https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/innodb-locks-set.html] (ie. those filtered by {{WHERE}}). In this particular case, the first query will lock all rows that need to be scanned, as determined by the execution plan - an index merge between {{status_idx}} and {{PRIMARY}} (regardless of the value of the {{provider_id}} column).

So, if both queries are executed at the exact same time they will both ask for locks on {{PRIMARY}} index and {{status_idx}} index. If the lock request order is not the same, then a deadlock occurs.

Sure, I’ll try to clarify this :)

{{Do I understand correctly that we may add the toll fee to a trip even when the driver may not need to pay it? 🤔 If so, I guess there is no way around this?}}

No, this should not happen. A toll road works as it’s a point A and B and one toll road can add fee if the connection is A to B and B to A. If the toll road only has a connection with A to B, and the drivers goes through it from B to A, fee is not added. But looking at the GPS it looks like the driver has crossed a toll road, but it’s here where it’s important to check the Toll road connection. 

Toll fee is calculated into the final price, so if they submit a PR it would make sens to first check if the driver has crossed a Toll road connection that should had a fee added to it. I don’t know the practise agents do this now, but if the agents where to just look at the GPS, it could give wrong outcome. 

_(If this is confusing or poorly explained, sorry if it is, it could make sens to have a quick call where I can show this more clearly and explain it)_  

In the example from Kaspar, the toll fee has been calculated into the final price, as the route includes fee. The driver did take a different route to the destination, where he entered through no toll roads, so the final price should not include a toll fee. The estimated price was 191 whereas the final price were 179. Which is then Final price 191 - Tollroad 12kr = 179. So if the driver then does a PR, he should not get the toll fee added. If the drivers does not submitted PR, the final price should be correct, with no added fee.

Lando setup:

* Lando requires Docker for Desktop (which requires a license, and we’re avoiding it in favor of Colima), and strongly depends on it, so some prerequisite steps are necessary 

Steps:

# Create a generic plist file at /Applications/Docker.app/Contents/Info.plist which contains at least a CFBundleShortVersionString key with value 4.9.1, this is the version validated by Lando, and if it’s missing, it will crash
# Create a (soft) symlink from the Colima’s socket (at ~/.colima/docker.sock) to /var/run/docker.sock, this is the route hardcoded in Lando

JURNAL

# Late Friday, Monday - started transitioning it to Colima instead of Docker Desktop - lando was crashing for any command - after extensive debugging, and taking a look in the source code of lando cli, found the problem to be in the way lando checks for docker version: it checks for the Info.plist file of Docker for Desktop app
# Monday - lando was not crashing anymore, but was failing in its try to start docker - it wasn’t able to find the socket - creating a symlink from Colima’s docker socket to the place where Docker for desktop socket is expected to live - solved the problem
# Late Monday - Tuesday - the first tries in starting the system - first problem found: there seemed to be a problem with the container names, they were generated with dashes (-) in name, but when they were checked to be up, the name that was searched for was with underscores (_), so it would fail every time - managed to bypass this by manually renaming containers after they were started
# Tuesday - Running the start command was always failing for the guidestyle container, and for the main Wordpress container - the service was returning either a blank page or a 404 error (probably generated by the traefik proxy)
# Tuesday - Wednesday - thought that the problem was for the theme not being build so started building the theme multiple times, always the same reason for fail: dns resolution for [storage.googleapis.com|http://storage.googleapis.com] was failing whilst installing a npm module - so I started investigating that - found out that’s a sub dependency that tries to download some core of chromium - started investigating the dns resolver - it was set to 127.0.0.11 (docker’s embedded dns resolver - used for internal networks), and was responding right for any domain (including [googleapis.com|http://googleapis.com], or other subdomains), but was failing for [storage.googleapis.com|http://storage.googleapis.com])
# Wednesday - Thursday: After an update of Colima and a temporary window in which it worked in a test container, the problem resurfaced when starting lando. Found as a forced solution forcing a new entry in the hosts file describing the IP of [storage.googleapis.com|http://storage.googleapis.com]. Following this update, all went good and the fail in the installation of dependencies in styleguide was now.. just moved later in the process. Whilst this, the main wp service seemed to be working, but two scenarios would happen:
## Either without a `lando install` at beginning, trying to enter the page at [bolt-food.lndo.site|http://bolt-food.lndo.site] would bring a wp installation page, which, at the end would let us successfully install a new clean version of wp - but the landing page would show the following error: “Theme not found”, and some of the repo files would be changed (the site name) - which led me thinking this is not expected to happen, and the installation should be handled automatically
## With lando install, Wordpress files would be generated, but accessing the /wp path would get an unstyled page

🗒️ *Monthly planning*

[~accountid:5cfa2e89757e4b0f2636ebf7] these are my notes when I started thinking that monthly Confluence pages don’t serve their purpose anymore; maybe you’ll find it useful.

*Why we use Confluence for monthly planning:*

* To make the plans transparent.
* To show the team a difference between first and second priority tasks.
* To do a monthly reflection.

*Why are monthly Confluence pages problematic:*

* Confluence pages now mostly include what we already have in Jira, thus creating duplication.
* Team members often forget to update the page at the end of the month:
** which makes this look like a chore rather than a reflection activity
** they already update their tasks in Jira so updating them again in Confluence seems unnecessary
* These pages are used only by our team > if someone else is interested, they can get access to Jira; in the last year, there was 0 such interest.
* If we need to set first and secondary priorities, we can still do it in Jira by using _low_ and _high_ priority labels (avoiding _medium_).
* Although these pages seemed useful in the beginning, they still don’t make a connection between team’s main goals and individual monthly tasks.

*What can we do differently:*

* Use OKR Jira plugin if possible to set monthly/quarterly team OKRs or use team yearly objectives and connect those to individual tasks.
* If the above is not possible, we can simply stop using Confluence and:
** plan everything in Jira
** use priority labels _low_ and _high_
** rely on team OKRs and operating principles when preparing monthly plans
** use Monday meetings at the beginning of a month to remind the team about the OKRs, main monthly goals, and how their work for that month connects to operating principles.

Hi Kaspar,

Double-checked this with the Safety team:

* Cases when the user reports a vehicle being faulty, without giving details on the reason why and does not mention anything about it being dangerous, would not be considered safety cases
* All other cases will be considered safety ones.

I also checked about the speed issues specifically; will quote their answer here:

{quote}Even though a “not accelerating” Scooter seems to be less dangerous than a stuck throttle that potentially can’t be slowed down, I think we should treat these cases as Safety cases. In the new workflow with FST this wouldn’t be an issue, as they simply add the problem marker and can thank the user for notifying us\!{quote}

I have updated the relevant articles accordingly:

* [🛴 User complains about scooter or e-bike features|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360018110920]
* [🛴 User reports technical issue with a scooter or e-bike|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/6569115410834]
* [🚨🛴 User reports a faulty scooter or e-bike|https://beehive.bolt.eu/main/kb/articles/internal/4901237473298]
* [🛴 Scooter rider issues list|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360020811560].

As for the compensation for the safety cases, you can follow these points:

* If the rider already unlocked the rental (and was charged), but discovered that the rental cannot be used, issue them a refund
* If the rider already took the trip and then complained, issue a refund based on the severity of the case
** For example, if the rider had to finish their trip earlier due to the rental being faulty, it would be fair to refund the charges
** If the rider took the ride with no issues but then discovered the rental was faulty and just informed us about it, there would not be a need for a refund.

Let me know if there are still some aspects that cause any confusion.

Hi Noud,

the context of this is that in order to escape framing of “robo-firing” of drivers, we introduced a human review into Driver Score feature so that long-lasting decision (to block a driver from platform) is made automatically but always by human intervention.

If we would drop human-review step, there is a high likelihood that driver blocking based on Driver Score would be seen as prohibited automated decision making under GDPR - which is the trigger for “robo-firing” framing. 

Though indeed I do see and agree that this is labour intensive with no other value besides “legal protection” being brought in. So all in all I see few potential out of this:

# *prolonging review timeline*

Trying to batch all reviews into  few weekly bathces for efficiency. Which would essentially mean that we cannot keep the 2-day promise and would keep drivers suspended for longer periods before making a “human-call” if to block or unblock.

BUT we would need to take guidance from Privacy team ([~accountid:609f85c547ba02006fe1b9c3] ) how much can we prolong the review term (if at all) for the auto-suspension for review not to be seen as prohibited robo-block in itself.

*2. Removing driver block as sanction altogether*

How much value does the blocking create in general? If there a case to be made that value from Driver Score blocks is lesser than investment on review?

We are doing this in UK given the negative framing of driver blocking based on quality in general. Since NL is still a Rides 2.0 market (aka high reclass-risk market) this approach would be useful and welcome in NL to fight reclass as well. I guess it is for [~accountid:619df38fc75da8007295630e]  to share his views/thoughts

*3. Finding an “outsource” arrangement where central team / external service providers do the human-review*

if costs are too high in one place - shift them to a low-cost place. Afterall there is no real reason for the reviews to happen on the ground in NL as it is mostly checking validity of signals based on detailed guidance. This is for   Sten and Lucas to thing about i suppose.

And [~accountid:609f85c547ba02006fe1b9c3]  maybe it is worth once again critically to re-asses the privacy guidance on a need to have human review involved (so the DPIA done earlier).



Hope this makes some sesne.

J,

{code:sql}with first_push as (
select user_id, min(created) first_push, count(created) push_count 
from ext_rental.rental_notification_push_notification
where created_date>'2022-01-01'
and type = 'order_bad_parking'
group by 1
)
select 
	case 
		when week_since_first_push in (0) then 'initial week'
		when week_since_first_push in (1,2,3,4) then '1-4 weeks'
		when week_since_first_push in (5,6,7,8) then '5-8 weeks'
		when week_since_first_push in (9,10,11,12) then '9-12 weeks'
		when week_since_first_push in (13,14,15,16) then '13-16 weeks'
		else 'other'
	end week_group,
sum(bad_parking),
sum(good_parking)+sum(failed_recognition)+sum(bad_parking),
1.0*sum(bad_parking)/(sum(good_parking)+sum(failed_recognition)+sum(bad_parking))
from (
select 
	t.user_id, 
	date_trunc('week',created) week_ts, 
	first_push,
	push_count,
	datediff('week',date_trunc('week',first_push),date_trunc('week',created)) week_since_first_push,
	count(case when model_response = 'good_parking' then id else null end) good_parking,
	count(case when model_response = 'bad_parking' then id else null end) bad_parking,
	count(case when model_response is  null then id else null end) failed_recognition
from rental.rental_order_bad_parking_detection_task t 
join first_push fp on t.user_id = fp.user_id
--where city_id=329
group by 1,2,3,4,5	
order by 1 asc, 2 asc
)
where 
	week_since_first_push >=0
	--and push_count < 10
group by 1
order by 1 asc
{code}

There are few types of problem here.  I noticed there are payments with type business. Let me describe that issue:
1) When we store paymentData we use client type came from paymentProfile. Schema is below.

!image-20220712-213159.png|width=75%!

In our case, paymentData came with {{"virtual_target_account":}}"72513218" ([example|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/partner-payments-payment/paymentData/view/47430565?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn]) and we use mentioned account to find payment profile. In our case it’s [3 SEPA Ride Hailing|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/partner-payments-payment-profile/paymentProfiles/3/assignments?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn]. LT : ride_hailing and EE : ride_hailing are assigned on that profile, so our system set client type = ride_hailing for mentioned paymentData. 

2) When we store payment we face inconsistency of client types. The root cause of that is demonstrated on schema below. We define the route based on fetched data from payment_data table, but then we recalculate client type based on reference number. 

!image-20220712-215939.png|width=66.66666666666666%!

In our case in the payment_data table the raw has  client type = ride_hailing so PaymentRoutingManager makes decision to use Ride Hailing route, but after that we recalculate client type based on reference number. In our case the reference number is 1010000000810548, it means our client type calculated based on ref number is Business. The system stores raw in payment table with client type = Business.

The chart should not be wider than the screen, so that is the problem.

Our current definition of driver quality, which is being calculated by the Driver Score, consists in:

* Driver Cancellation
* Rider Ratings
* Rider Tickets

During the Driver Score tests, we were able to see improvement on these metrics and we believe it’s related to two things:

# Giving drivers more feedback about what we expect from them.
# Incentivize them by the fear of punishment, which is the block.

But, we want to validate if this is true. We want to understand why they are improving their behavior and I believe we will be able to do that soon.

We have started three weeks ago a test in Birmingham. Due to legal reasons, we won’t block drivers in the UK, just offering guidance. In this AB test, we will be able to compare not only the Driver Score vs Rating difference, but also compare their behavior with other markets in which we have the blocks in place. If the fear of pushing is not really changing their behavior, we may offer the same approach to the Netherlands.

*Identified one more related problem (the 3rd and I hope the last)*We use 2 tables in conjunction to store order profiling results:

* order_check
* order_check_result

{{order_check_result}} table stores a type of profiling query which marks order
{{order_check_result}} table references order_check table by order_check.idThe problem is in following:

* {{order_check_result}} table doesn’t store city_id and order_id (unique order key)
* it relies on data in {{order_check}}  table (this table has city_id and order_id + many other data columns)
* We insert data into {{order_check}}  table, when driver finishes order (explicitly pushes button in driver app)
* I guess that this profiling query searches for case orders where driver goes offline at some point during the order. So, driver doesn’t finish order explicitly and we don’t have data about this order in {{order_check}}  table
* Due to the fact above and the way we store order profiling results => profiling results for this profiling strategy is not stored in DB

For the moment I don’t have quick solution for this.
It will take some time to re-design and fix this problem
(generally, I think we should store city_id and order_id in {{order_check_result}} table and JOIN tables by city_id and order_id)

I’ve spoken to Martin about tolls and PRs and assessed the impact, here are my thoughts:

* As drivers can reach a cap for toll roads, they won’t necessarily have to pay it on every trip that passes one, so we should keep the 🇳🇴 Driver Compensation Guidelines as they are and not provide any compensation to drivers for toll fees.
* If the driver has submitted a PR, Martin has said we could close it with the Upfront price. However, I thought about this some more and we should:
** a) Be frugal and only pay the driver (and charge the rider) for the toll fee if they actually went through the toll
** b) Educate the driver about why the price is less, so we can reduce contact about the same thing in future, and also not end up with too many PRs
** c) Encourage the driver to take the suggested route if they want to ensure they will get the quoted price
* In the ticket example that you gave, it seems that it was not properly explained to the driver about the route change, which resulted in the trip price being lower.

*As for updates to the KB:*

I think nothing is needed for the NO Compensation Guidelines. As for 🚗 Completing a Price Review, I’m currently trying to confirm if drivers can see the comment that’s left in the PR - if yes, we can use this to educate the driver. 

In general though, the process seems correct and we should perhaps just remind the CS team that if the driver took a different route and submits a PR, then we follow the process as per 🚗  Completing a Price Review and do not adjust the price to the Upfront amount, nor do we add any toll fees if they didn’t go through them.

Hey\!

The previous privacy guidance still stands as human 2 day review is essential in order this activity not to fall under GDPR art 22 (automated individual decision making). 

If we would lose the human review, then this automatically means that this processing activity is deemed as automated decision making and Article 22(1) sets out a general prohibition on such decision-making. The only exception would be that this processing is necessary for the performance of the contract, but this is interpreted very strictly and there is high likelihood that this processing activity would not fall under this exception. 

Therefore the 2 days review is really essential and I advise keeping this for all EU markets where GDPR is applicable. 

# *Prolonging the review period.* The length of time that the impact persists is relevant to assess whether it imposes a “significant effect on the data subject”. The more serious an impact is, the less time it would take to be considered significant. In the view of depriving a person of their income over a short period of time could be itself considered significant and therefore fall under art 22. SO → I don’t see much room here to prolong the period as well. 
# *Removing the suspension/block.* With this option privacy concern would fall away, no human review needed.

Testing scenarios:

# City has *batch_only_same_provider* off, provider has it on => courier should *not* be assigned a batch
# City has *batch_only_same_provider* off, provider has it off => courier should be assigned a batch
# City has *batch_only_same_provider* on, provider has it on => courier should *not* be assigned a batch
# City has *batch_only_same_provider* on, provider has it off => courier should *not* be assigned a batch

Provider specific toggle for *batch_only_same_provider* can be found in provider profile / info tab / courier setup section, just below *batching enabled* toggle.

In case there are issues with the case where both are tuned off and the batched should be created, try changing city level and/or provider level batching settings to less restrictive values.

Hi Mari,

in principle, where possible we are recommending keeping data residence within the EEA.

Under GDPR, any transfer of personal data is subject to additional requirements such as entering into agreement specifically on international data transfer and performing data transfer impact assessment to ensure that the level of the data protection in the recipient’s country will be essentially equivalent to that ensured within the EU. As data transfers to the US in general are currently under regulatory scrutiny (see recent decisions in the EU stating non-compliance of Google Analytics transferring data to the US due to the insufficient safeguards), there is a risk that at some point this transfer would be deemed unlawful by the regulator. This however would affect not only Bolt but all data exporters and will force both vendors and its clients to find alternative solutions.

Given that we don’t have 100% certainty how this will transpire on the regulatory level going forward, this is ultimately a business decision. There is some inherent privacy risk attached to choosing to store data in the US, however if the supplier proposition is unique and you factor in the possibility that at some point we might need to make adjustments in terms of the data residency, then from privacy perspective we can help to reduce (but not eliminate) the risk by concluding Standard Contractual Clauses and engaging our InfoSec team to check security standard of this vendor.

Best regards,

Adriana

In the request, Police are citing point 10, article 105 from OUG 195/2002, which states:

Article 105. _The following acts committed by legal entities are considered offences and are sanctioned with the fine provided in the fifth class of sanctions:_

_10) non-compliance with the obligation to communicate, within the term indicated in the request of the traffic police, the identification data of the person to whom they entrusted the vehicle to drive on public roads, provided in art. 39_

And article 39 from the same law states the following:

_1)  At the request of the traffic police, the owner or the authorized holder of a vehicle is obliged to communicate to it, within the term indicated in the request, the identification data of the person to whom he entrusted the vehicle to drive on public roads._

_2) The obligation to communicate the identification data, provided at point (1), shall be deemed to be fulfilled if the owner or the authorized holder of a vehicle communicates the name, surname, personal identification code, domicile or residence, number and series of the identity document of the person to whom it entrusted the vehicle to drive on public roads or, in case foreign nationals, stateless persons or Romanian citizens residing abroad, the series and number of the passport or other document crossing the state border, the date of its issuance and the issuing state._

Hi all,
I have only received this ticket today, so I wasn’t aware of it before.


NL is obviously a market where, in general, the risk of reclassification of _independent_ drivers is very high and the legal situation is somewhat uncertain.


However, I understand from the terms of this contract that the drivers will actually be _employed_ by the Fleet Partner and therefore work as salaried drivers of the Fleet Partner. If that is indeed the case, there should be no particular risk of reclassification of those drivers as they are employees already. 


The risk that those fleet employees be considered employees of the platform, i.e. Bolt, is relatively low - in the Dutch regulatory context, what matters for the trade union is that drivers fall under the collective labour agreement for taxi drivers. This is already the case in this setup. These has been no discussion so far about whether employees of fleets  should be ‘reclassified’ as employees of the platform. 
 
Best regards,
Marc

One main point in the idea of interleaving tests is that we use one platform (the one we consider 'control') to model the dynamics of the 'test' platform as if we did not decrease the costs there.

But there are two difficulties to it:

*First:*

This idea of interleaving tests takes the assumption that both platforms have the same dynamics. But it looks like it's not always true.

Let's look at the dynamics of a week's android and ios dymamics as if it were experiment. We then take the first day of the experiment as the base and compare other days to it.

!Screenshot 2022-07-15 at 00.36.19.png|width=1728,height=1117!



_Below are more simulations for install (upper-funnel) and some simulations for First Ride (lower-funnel)_

[^2022-05-13_install.csv]
[^2022-04-20_install.csv]
[^2022-03-14_install.csv]
[^2022-02-05_install.csv]
[^2022-05-13_First Ride Finished.csv]
[^2022-04-20_First Ride Finished.csv]
[^2022-03-14_First Ride Finished.csv]
[^2022-02-05_First Ride Finished.csv]

One can see that difference between android and ios dynamics can be up to 10 percent points (and sometimes even in different directions). This difference happens without any cost intervention. So, in an experiment setting we could wrongly attribute this difference to ads.

*Can we overcome it?*

Yes, we can actually model the behaviour of android and ios. E.g. from the data we can see that ios is more responsive to seasonality than android, so we could make a model, predicting android's values based on ios and vice versa.

*But.* We already have incrmntal (external provider) that actually already does counterfactual modelling.

*Second:*

If ads do have effect, decreasing the cost only on one platform might not bring visible results. If we decrease the cost on ios, but continue spending on android, the users with ios see lot's of Bolt cars still being used by android users and continue using Bolt.

In this way we do not entirely remove the ads from ios users. In this ways it's better to remove all of the ads and model total amount event we would normally achieve (as we can do with incremental). This will make the effect be more visible.

Copy data to new EBS scenario

* Add data volume to instances with `data_volume = 1800` and apply
* Enable `create_data_volume: true` in group_vars
* Change ansible slightly

```diff
diff --git a/roles/kafka/tasks/createDataVolume.yaml b/roles/kafka/tasks/createDataVolume.yaml
index 7b899c47..ac8ae196 100644
--- a/roles/kafka/tasks/createDataVolume.yaml
+++ b/roles/kafka/tasks/createDataVolume.yaml
@@ -64,7 +64,7 @@
 
 - name: Create a directory /data if it doesn't exist
   file:
-    path: /data
+    path: /opt/data
     state: directory
     owner: kafka
     group: kafka
@@ -72,7 +72,7 @@
 
 - name: Mount up data device by label
   mount:
-    path: /data
+    path: /opt/data
     src: LABEL=data
     fstype: ext4
     state: mounted
diff --git a/roles/kafka/tasks/main.yaml b/roles/kafka/tasks/main.yaml
index f8cd070d..8d8390f3 100644
--- a/roles/kafka/tasks/main.yaml
+++ b/roles/kafka/tasks/main.yaml
@@ -34,7 +34,7 @@
 
 - name: Get datadir status
   stat:
-    path: /data
+    path: /opt/data
   register: datadir
 
 - include_tasks: createDataVolume.yaml
```

* run it, new EBS will be prepared and mounted to /opt/data
* stop kafka service `systemctl stop kafka`
* Install rsync `apt-get install rsync` and [run](https://serverfault.com/a/505758) `time rsync -ahW --info=progress2 --no-compress /data/kafka/ /opt/data/kafka`


```log
$ time rsync -ahW --info=progress2 --no-compress /data/kafka/ /opt/data/kafka

real    14m12.564s
Size 76Gb, volumes GP3 both source/dest
```

* `mkdir -p /opt/data-backup`
* `mv /data/kafka/ /opt/data-backup/`
* `umount /opt/data`
* change mountpoint for data in `vim /etc/fstab`
* `mount /data`, check `df -h /data` that new volume is used
* start kafka back to test copy was done correctly, check in-sync status (took 6 min to sync 20Gb from other brokers after rsync to new volume)
* wait till all synced
* stop kafka, redeploy instance with smaller root volume (enable `delete_on_termination = false` in instance module before to keep old EBS)
* don't forget to remove changes from kafka role before provisioning new instance
* also, remove separate kafka user as well (kafka1-3) to use generic one
* after provision, all data will be mounted back to /data, and broker will resync all changes
* old volume will be left with the same name, so it could be used as backup in case of problems

Some takeaways:

* avoid using clicks (less signal)
* avoid using costs (different effectiveness for each cent spent)
* for promotions - dummy variables (if not measurable)
* for specific events - dummy
* for seasons - temperature (but I am not sure)

recommended window - 2 years back
(But one can set the model up, so it evaluates trend and seasonality on larger dataset and uses more recent data for other things))

recommended external variables to add: GDP growth, unemployment, inflation

Model channels differently and try to be more granular

if not enough variation and volume in a variable - exclude it

Having daily data is acceptable for granularity, but weekly sometimes can be better, since daily data have lots of noise (but check for data sparsity)

Define big impactful channels with more granularity

How choose between multiple collinear predictors? (Ridge?)

data("dt_prophet_holidays") + customize carry over and prior impact

Alternatively, if good quality data has been collected to explain certain different holidays and events, this can be modelled as a specific independent variable and turn off the holiday option in Prophet.

In Robyn you can control sign of coefficients

paid media and organic go for data transformations (adstock and saturating bahaviour)
context vars do not apply data transformations

factor_vars for categorical data

Prefer continuous data to provide variation

Check:
Michaelis Menten function, Spend exposure plot for spend-exposure relationship

Use spend instead of imps if impressions perform poorly even after splitting and giving exrta granularity

Adstock - modelling that ads do not have immediate effect - the effects of advertising can lag and decay following an initial exposure

Saturation = decreasing ads utility = each additional unit of advertising exposure increases the response, but at a declining rate

adstock and decay modelling:
[https://facebookexperimental.github.io/Robyn/docs/features/#variable-transformations|https://facebookexperimental.github.io/Robyn/docs/features/#variable-transformations|smart-link]
